messages:
Alice: Customer report: requests to our /v1/generate returning 403 only when routed via their PrivateLink NLB+TGW path. Works from internet. Happened after they migrated a subnet to TGW.
Bob: Can you paste a failing curl output and the resolved IP for api.redwood.example from inside their VPC?
Alice: From their pod:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example
10.0.34.12

$ curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
* Connected to 10.0.34.12 (10.0.34.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake completed without SNI
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"access_denied","message":"request unauthorized"}
```
Bob: "TLS handshake completed without SNI" looks suspicious. If the NLB is doing TLS passthrough and not forwarding SNI to downstream ALB/hosts we can hit Host-based routing/auth checks.
Carol: Also ask customer to check VPCE policy and SG egress. If VPCE endpoint policy restricts allowed principals or actions it can yield 403 from our auth layer if headers are rewritten.
Dave: Quick checks:
- aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-xxx (confirm PolicyDocument)
- check endpoint SGs allow 443 outbound to our NLB
- ensure Route table for subnet points to TGW/VPCE correctly

Alice: They ran describe-vpc-endpoints, policy looks wide open (Allow: execute-api:Invoke). SGs look permissive. Route tables show route to TGW -> Transit VPC -> endpoint.
InfraBot: Suggest packet capture on the instance hitting 10.0.34.12: tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/pl.pcap then share.
Alice: They attached pcap excerpt. Highlights: Client hello lacks SNI extension when traffic arrives at our NLB IP.
Carol: Why would SNI be stripped? Possible causes: onprem proxy, intermediate TLS terminator, or the NLB configured as TCP listener terminating TLS at backend without preserving SNI. Also some older TLS proxies don't forward SNI when doing re-encryption.
Bob: Could be TGW/Transit VPC appliance doing TLS inspection (decrypt + re-encrypt) and failing to set SNI on re-encrypt. Ask if they have a firewall or NGFW in the transit path with TLS inspection.
Alice: Customer says they do have a Palo Alto in the transit account doing TLS inspect for egress. They confirmed it's set to re-encrypt but default profile didn't preserve SNI for certain flows.
Dave: That matches. Our auth layer uses SNI + Host header validation for tenant routing when traffic hits the NLB. If SNI missing, backend chooses default vhost which isn't authorized and returns 403.
Carol: Short-term workaround: have them add a conditional resolver rule so api.redwood.example resolves to the VPCE private IP but route traffic directly (bypass TLS-inspection) or add an allowlist for our host on the fw to disable inspect for that FQDN.
Alice: We've suggested two options to customer:
1) Disable TLS inspect for api.redwood.example FQDN or create a passthrough rule so SNI is preserved.
2) Configure their Transit proxy to include SNI on re-encrypt or use TLS passthrough to the NLB.
3) As a fallback, we can add an explicit vhost for the IP path to accept Host-only requests (but that weakens host-based routing; needs infra approval).
Bob: For traceability, ask them to test curl with `--resolve` to bypass their DNS and hit our public ip path vs private to confirm difference:
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.0.34.12 https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
```
Alice: They tried --resolve and still got 403 when going via proxy path. When they route directly to our public NLB (bypassing transit FW) it succeeds.
Dave: So root cause confirmed: TLS inspection appliance in transit re-encrypts without SNI. Customer needs to change inspection rule to preserve SNI or bypass for api.redwood.example.
Carol: Also recommended they add egress allowlist entry for our ALB/NLB IP ranges (we gave them list) and ensure X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Host headers are passed so our logs show original host IP for debugging.
Alice: Customer will adjust policy and test. I'll follow up once they change.
InfraBot: Escalation created: #INC-2026, assigned to network eng. Tagging @Dave for infra change if they want us to deploy the vhost fallback.
Dave: I can stand up a temporary vhost to accept host-only if customer cannot change FW quickly, but prefer they fix inspection rules.
Alice: Customer confirms change made, test shows success. They disabled inspect for the FQDN and requests through PrivateLink now return 200. Root cause: TLS inspection re-encrypt without SNI. Closing after 24h observation.
Bob: Nice. Add a KB note: "PrivateLink/TGW transit + TLS inspection may strip SNI -> 403. Verify SNI in client hello and bypass or preserve in re-encrypt." :white_check_mark:
Alice: Adding ticket notes and KB. :thumbsup:"
